page: The Amazon Web Services x8i.16xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated 32-core, 64-thread Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at up to 3.9 GHz, based on the x86_64 architecture. Memory provisioning stands at 1024.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 RAM operating at 7 GHz, delivering an expansive memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16 GB per core. Compute capabilities are augmented by hardware instruction sets including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512, supported by a 480 MB L3 cache. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 30 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included. The instance does not include bundled local instance storage, requiring attached network volumes for persistent data.

Across synthetic and real-world benchmarks, the instance demonstrates robust compute and cache performance. Multi-core performance is particularly capable, with Geekbench multi-core (20,822.0) and software compilation using Clang (59,178.0) ranking in the top ten percent of cloud instances. Cached memory bandwidth on small blocks reaches 5104.32 GB/sec, placing it in the top quartile, while PassMark database operations and Redis SET operations (113.79 million ops/sec) reflect high throughput for in-memory operational workloads. Similarly, static web serving reaches 106.03 GB/sec. Large language model inference prompt processing on smaller and medium parameter sizes tests in the top tier due to Intel AMX matrix acceleration, while token generation rates scale moderately on larger models.

The primary operational tradeoff involves memory bandwidth under uncached workloads and storage architecture. While cached memory operations exhibit high throughput, uncached large-block 256MB read and write bandwidth register in the middle fifty percent. Additionally, the lack of local NVMe SSD storage places complete dependence on Amazon EBS or networked file storage, shifting I/O economics and operational latencies to network-attached infrastructure. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high RAM density per compute core reduces the total virtual core count needed to host very large datasets, though it remains specialized for memory-bound tasks rather than disk-intensive streaming.

The AWS x8i.16xlarge is suited for in-memory data platforms, enterprise caching tiers such as Redis, large-footprint relational database instances, Clang-based distributed build farms, and memory-intensive analytical processing where full-dataset residency in DDR5 memory is critical.
description: The Amazon Web Services x8i.16xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the Nitro hypervisor and powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor. Configured with 32 physical cores and 64 dedicated vCPUs operating at 3.9 GHz, it features 1024 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz alongside a 480 MB L3 cache and AMX acceleration. The server delivers 30 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, contains no integrated GPUs, and includes no local instance storage. Benchmark results show top-tier multi-threaded compilation and small-block cached memory performance, accompanied by high-throughput Redis and database operational execution. However, large-block uncached memory operations achieve average speeds, and external storage is mandatory. The hardware configuration is tailored for large-scale in-memory databases, caching infrastructure, and memory-heavy enterprise analytics.
